Where it began

Shane Watson was born on 17 June 1981 and grew up in Ipswich, Queensland. He came up through the Brothers club in Ipswich and Eastern Suburbs in Brisbane, and played for Australia at the Under-19 World Cup in 2000.

That year a rule change at the national academy left him free to choose his state, and he headed south to Hobart, where Tasmania promised him a place straight away. He began at number seven and finished his first half-season at four, with a first-class hundred in only his fifth game. In 2004 he moved home to Queensland.

The player

He batted with real power and bowled at a brisk fast-medium pace, the kind of cricketer who lets a side carry an extra bowler. His Test debut came against Pakistan at Sydney in January 2005. In 59 Tests up to 2015 he scored 3,731 runs at 35.20, with four hundreds, 24 fifties and a best of 176, and took 75 wickets at 33.68, with a best of 6 for 33.

His finest Test years came as an opener alongside Simon Katich. He finished 2009 with a first Test hundred, 120 not out against Pakistan, and opened his 2010 tour of India with a patient 126 at Mohali. The Allan Border Medal came his way in 2010 and 2011. One afternoon against South Africa in November 2011 he needed just five overs to take 5 for 17.

What made him special

In white-ball cricket he could win a match on his own. He was named man of the match in the Champions Trophy finals of 2006 and 2009, collected World Cup winner's medals in 2007 and 2015, and was player of the tournament at the 2012 World Twenty20. His unbeaten 185 from 96 balls against Bangladesh in 2011 included 15 sixes. In 2016 he became the first Australian with an international hundred in all three formats, and he captained his country in each of them too.

Test hundreds, though, could be shy. Before that first Test hundred arrived he was out for 96, 89 and 93 in quick succession, and soon after it he fell for 97.

Away from the middle

He was twice player of the tournament in the IPL, in 2008 and 2013, and won the title with Rajasthan and later Chennai. After retiring in 2020 he turned to coaching. In 2019 he was elected President of the Australian Cricketers' Association.

He is married to the broadcaster Lee Furlong. He started a sports clinic, Let's Activate, that teaches youngsters the basics of movement and games, and he hosts a podcast, Lessons Learnt with the Greats. Oddly for a man who batted and bowled right-handed, he writes with his left.

And finally

On the 2005 tour of England the team stayed a night at Lumley Castle, which is said to be haunted. Watson took one look at his room and decided against it, spending the night on the floor of Brett Lee's room instead. A man happy to open the batting against anyone drew the line at ghosts.
